Pure query over current state (dp-09 refusal seam), which is exactly what selectDate() and handleRangeEnter() act on.

withToday(\DateTimeImmutable $today): selfPin the "today" reference (testability). Default (unset) uses the real wall-clock now, so production behavior is unchanged. Pinning also un-hides the marker if withoutToday() had hidden it (dp-33).
withoutToday(): selfHide the today marker entirely (dp-33 honest semantics): no cell renders with the today/selected-today style until withClockToday() restores the wall-clock anchor or withToday() pins a new one. Navigation by goToToday() still works while hidden — the date exists, only the marker is off.
withClockToday(): selfFollow the real wall clock as "today" again after withoutToday() — the state a freshly built picker starts in. The marker re-reads the clock on every render, so a session crossing midnight silently repaints a different today (no tick source, by design; dp-33 documentation flip).
todayHidden(): boolTrue while the today marker is hidden by withoutToday() (dp-33).
setTime(\DateTimeImmutable $t): self
moveToDate(\DateTimeImmutable $date): selfAim the cursor at an arbitrary date (the edit-existing-value recipe): when $date falls inside the currently viewed month the cursor lands on its cell; otherwise the view is unchanged and the cursor is re-aimed at the viewed month's FIRST SELECTABLE day (min/max consulted via firstValidIndex — the same "aim or reset to first valid" law the constructor and setTime follow). The cursor never keeps a stale position on an out-of-month jump: an off-screen cursor is worse than a reset one. Immutable.

DateRange final readonly class

Represents a date range with start and end dates.

MethodSummary
__construct(public ?\DateTimeImmutable $start = null, public ?\DateTimeImmutable $end = null)
static new(?\DateTimeImmutable $start = null, ?\DateTimeImmutable $end = null): selfHouse factory mirroring the constructor.
withStart(\DateTimeImmutable $start): self
withEnd(\DateTimeImmutable $end): self
contains(\DateTimeImmutable $date): bool
durationInDays(?\DateTimeImmutable $now = null): ?intWhole elapsed days between start and end — 2026-01-01 to 2026-01-03 returns 2, although the calendar span covers three days. The count is SIGNED: an inverted range (end before start) reports the negative elapsed figure — 2026-01-05 to 2026-01-01 returns -4, never a mirror +4 — so a consumer can tell "backwards" from "same instant". Membership deliberately disagrees: contains() treats an inverted range as empty (false everywhere); the sign is direction information, not an invitation to probe inside. With an open-ended range, $now supplies the closing date; it defaults to real wall-clock now so the pure-integer math stays testable without a clock injection when the caller wants the live figure.
isComplete(): bool
